speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of AIDS and the sudden onset of visual symptoms, it is crucial to determine if this is an opportunistic infection. When did these black spots and decreased vision first appear, and have you noticed any floaters or flashes of light?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of pain and your history of advanced AIDS raise strong suspicion for Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis, but we must rule out other causes. Have you noticed any pain with eye movement or changes in your vision field, such as a curtain coming down over your sight? I will now request an urgent dilated fundoscopic examination and CD4 count to confirm the diagnosis.

speaker: Patient
